official.deadline_note: Application window opens 1 December 2026 and closes 15 March 2027. Institutional deadlines differ from the programme's: each partner university sets its own admissions deadline, which can fall before the Fund's cut-off, and ROC (Taiwan) embassy/consulate first-review recommendations are due to the TaiwanICDF no later than 31 March each year.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake, fall semester only; applications open 1 December 2026 and close 15 March 2027
official.status_note: The Fund's official page states: 'The 2027 TaiwanICDF Scholarship applications open from December 1, 2026 to March 15, 2027!' and directs applicants to the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System (page updated 15 July 2026).
official.tuition_coverage_note: The TaiwanICDF will cover the tuition fee as required by the student's university; credit fees, which vary with the number of credits registered, will also be covered as required by the student's university.
benefits: The total scholarship, including airfare (round-trip), housing, tuition, credit fees, insurance, textbook costs and a monthly allowance will be provided by the TaiwanICDF to each student within his/her given award period.

Monthly allowance for food and miscellaneous living expenses, deposited monthly into the student's local bank account: NT$15,000 per month (Bachelor's Program), NT$18,000 per month (Master's Program), NT$20,000 per month (Ph.D. Program). The funding_amount recorded here is the Master's tier; Bachelor's and Ph.D. tiers differ.
Airfare: The TaiwanICDF shall arrange your most-direct flights to and from Taiwan with Economy Class tickets.
Housing: All students must reside in the student dormitories.
Tuition fee and credit fees: The TaiwanICDF will cover the tuition fee as required by the student's university, and credit fees will also be covered as required by the university.

Insurance fees will be covered for the entire duration of the program, in addition to the mandatory student safety insurance set by the Ministry of Education; textbook purchases as required by instructors are subject to the approval of the director of the student's institute.
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country on the List of Countries Eligible for TaiwanICDF Scholarship, and satisfy any specific criteria established by his or her country and/or government of citizenship.
Neither be a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan) nor an overseas compatriot student.
Satisfy the admission requirements of the partner university to which he or she has applied to study under a TaiwanICDF scholarship.

Be able to satisfy all requirements for a Resident Visa (Code: FS) set by the Bureau of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and an Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) set by the Ministry of the Interior of the ROC (Taiwan) government; the TaiwanICDF has the right to revoke a scholarship offered if an applicant cannot satisfy the visa requirements.

Upon accepting a TaiwanICDF scholarship, not hold any other ROC (Taiwan) government-sponsored scholarship (such as the Taiwan Scholarship) in the same academic year in which the TaiwanICDF scholarship would be due to commence.
Bachelor's programs are exclusively available to applicants from countries that maintain diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
requirements: Complete the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System in full; applicants must ensure that they submit accurate and complete information, and failure to do so will result in the application not being processed.
Applicants can only apply for one program at one TICA university each year, and must also submit a separate program application to the chosen university/program.
Fulfil the application procedures required by the university applied to and submit all documents required by the TaiwanICDF partner school before that university's admissions deadline.

Submit all required documents to the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative Office in the home country if necessary; whether hard or soft copies are required depends on the decision of each individual office.

Provide the highest-level diploma before the Fund's stated July cut-off (July 31, 2026 for the 2026 cycle); applicants unable to obtain the certificate by this date may instead apply for next year's scholarship.

Applicants who have already held a TaiwanICDF scholarship, MOFA's Taiwan Scholarship or an MOE scholarship must have graduated before the Fund's stated cut-off (before July 31, 2025 for the 2026 cycle).
documents: Completed online application in the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System, containing accurate and complete information.
Highest-level diploma, which must be obtainable before the Fund's stated July cut-off date.
All admission documents required by the chosen TaiwanICDF partner university, submitted before that university's admissions deadline (see the Fund's 'Programs Available for Application' document).
Whatever hard or soft copies the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative Office in the applicant's country requires.
A signed consent form, returned to the TaiwanICDF through the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Representative Office after the acceptance letter is received.
selection_criteria: First review: the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative office reviews applicants based on the eligibility requirements and selection criteria of the TaiwanICDF and sends its list of recommended applicants to the TaiwanICDF no later than March 31 each year.

Second review: an academic committee organized by the individual partner university in joint cooperation with TaiwanICDF representatives reviews qualified applicants based on the university's selection criteria, whilst also accounting for the eligibility requirements and selection criteria of the TaiwanICDF.
The Fund evaluates all applicants comprehensively rather than accepting or rejecting them based on one single quality; all positive features are valued and there is no age limit.
coverage: Round-trip airfare: most-direct flights to and from Taiwan with Economy Class tickets, arranged by the TaiwanICDF.
Housing: residence in the student dormitories.
Tuition fee and credit fees as required by the student's university.
Insurance: mandatory student safety insurance plus accidental and necessary medical coverage, with fees covered for the entire duration of the program.
Textbook costs as required by instructors, subject to the approval of the director of the student's institute.
Monthly allowance for food and miscellaneous living expenses: NT$15,000 (Bachelor's) / NT$18,000 (Master's) / NT$20,000 (Ph.D.) per month, deposited monthly into the student's local bank account.
application_method: Complete the online application at the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System during the window of December 1, 2026 to March 15, 2027.
Submit a separate program application to the chosen TICA partner university and meet its admission requirements before its admissions deadline.
Deliver the required documents to the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative Office in the home country where necessary.

Pass the embassy/consulate first review (recommendation list due to the Fund by March 31) and the university academic committee's second review conducted in cooperation with TaiwanICDF representatives.

Receive the acceptance letter issued by the TaiwanICDF (announced, in principle, no later than June 10) through the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative Office, then return a signed consent form to accept.
official.application_route: Apply online through the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System, submit a separate admission application to the chosen TICA partner university, and route required documents via the ROC (Taiwan) embassy, consulate general or representative office in the applicant's country.
official.study_mode: Degree programmes at TICA partner universities with fall-semester admission only; one listed master's programme (E-Learning Master Program of Education and School Leadership, National Chung Cheng University) is conducted online except the first-semester orientation and fourth-semester thesis oral defense.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be citizens of countries on the Fund's List of Countries Eligible for TaiwanICDF Scholarship and satisfy any specific criteria of their country/government; nationals of the ROC (Taiwan) and overseas compatriot students are excluded. Bachelor's programmes are exclusively for applicants from countries that maintain diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme exists for nationals of Taiwan's eligible partner and diplomatic countries to study in Taiwan; applicants from non-beneficiary countries are not eligible to apply.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: One programme at one Taiwan International Cooperation Alliance (TICA) partner university per year; the eligible programmes for each cycle are published by the Fund in 'Programs Available for Application'.
official.duration: The duration of the funded programme; the Fund states the scholarship cannot be extended and any additional period of study must be taken at the student's own expense.
official.description: The International Higher Education Scholarship Program, central to the TaiwanICDF, offers full scholarships to outstanding students from partner countries to pursue higher education in Taiwan through collaborations with local universities under the Taiwan International Cooperation Alliance (TICA), with the stated goal of supporting the socio-economic growth of partner countries through the cultivation of highly talented individuals.
official.english_requirement: The TaiwanICDF has no requirements regarding English proficiency test; applicants must follow the policies of the school and program applied to, which may include academic or language requirements such as an English proficiency test. All training is conducted in English, and applicants should contact the school or programme for further guidance.

not_confirmed: Research-proposal requirement: the Fund publishes no research-proposal requirement for this scholarship.
A single itemised document checklist: the Fund does not publish one central list; admission documents are set per programme by each partner university in 'Programs Available for Application'.
Programme-by-programme duration in months: the Fund states the award period is that of the funded programme but publishes no lengths in the guidebook.

The 2027-cycle edition of the guidebook: the latest published edition is the 2026 guidebook (v3.0, January 2026), so cycle-specific cut-off dates such as the July 31 diploma and prior-scholarship graduation dates will shift for the 2027 round.
verification.notes: Stipend tiers (NT$15,000/18,000/20,000 per month), coverage items and eligibility rules were read directly from the Fund's own Scope of Scholarship 2026 PDF and the 2026 Application Guidebook v3.0; the 2027 window (1 Dec 2026 - 15 Mar 2027) was taken from the programme and Apply Now pages, both updated 15 July 2026. The TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System portal (web.icdf.org.tw/ICDF_TSP) could not be reached for a live check from this environment; every recorded value comes from the www.icdf.org.tw pages fetched live.

applicant_utility.summary: This is one of the few genuinely full awards for Taiwan: round-trip economy airfare, dormitory housing, tuition and credit fees, insurance, approved textbooks, and a monthly living stipend of NT$15,000 (bachelor's), NT$18,000 (master's) or NT$20,000 (PhD) paid into a Taiwanese bank account. The 2027 window runs 1 December 2026 to 15 March 2027, but your earliest binding date is usually the partner university's own admissions deadline, which can fall sooner. Each applicant gets exactly one programme at one TICA university for the whole cycle, and the TaiwanICDF sets no English test of its own - yet a university admission does not mean funding; only the Fund's acceptance letter, expected in principle by 10 June, confirms the award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year undergraduates and recent graduates from Taiwan's listed partner countries who can decide early on one English-taught degree and who need travel, housing and living costs covered.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the Fund's eligible-country list first; if it is not listed, this scholarship is closed to you regardless of your grades.

Pick one programme from the current 'Programs Available for Application' document, then check that university's own admissions deadline and language policy - the 15 March date is the Fund's cut-off, not the university's.
Draft the online application in the first weeks of the December window, because the Fund will not process inaccurate or incomplete submissions at all.
Contact your ROC (Taiwan) embassy, consulate general or representative office before March to confirm whether they want paper or digital copies and what they need.
If you have held a prior TaiwanICDF, MOFA or MOE scholarship, check the graduation cut-off; if your diploma will be issued after the late-July cut-off, plan to apply in the next cycle.
common_rejection_risks: Treating a university admission offer as the scholarship decision - admitted but unfunded applicants are the classic failure here.
Meeting the Fund's 15 March deadline but missing the partner university's earlier admissions deadline.
Submitting an online form with inaccurate or incomplete information, which the Fund says will not be processed.
Applying for a bachelor's programme from a country that does not maintain diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
Holding or accepting another ROC government scholarship such as the Taiwan Scholarship in the same academic year.
Expecting a spring start or a deferral - only fall admission is offered and deferring the award is not allowed.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Applicants still fund personal spending beyond the monthly food-and-miscellaneous allowance, any fees or expenses the chosen school or programme charges outside tuition and credit fees (each school and programme may set its own policies), personal travel and incidentals, and any study beyond the award period, since the scholarship cannot be extended and additional study is at the student's own expense.
document_audit: The Fund does not require recommendation letters, but the university frequently does - read the programme's own admission requirements, not just the guidebook FAQ.
Textbook purchases need the institute director's approval, so treat books as reimbursed-on-approval rather than a guaranteed budget.
Embassies and representative offices individually decide whether hard or soft copies are required, so confirm your local office's format instead of assuming one package works everywhere.
Your highest-level diploma must be obtainable by the Fund's late-July cut-off; a degree conferred after that date pushes you into the next cycle.
There is no application fee for the online form, but the university may charge its own - check before paying anything.
alerts: The window opens 1 December 2026 and closes 15 March 2027 - earlier than most Taiwan government scholarship schemes, so gather documents before December.
Embassy first-review recommendations are due to the Fund around 31 March, so document delivery to your representative office cannot wait for the final day either.
One shot per year: one programme, one university, no changes after submission, and switching TICA programmes after acceptance cancels the scholarship.
Results are announced in principle by 10 June, with acceptance letters delivered through your ROC (Taiwan) embassy or representative office rather than directly.
Part-time work is permitted within Taiwan employment law and can supplement the fixed stipend, but no second Taiwan-government-funded scholarship is allowed while you hold this one.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the TaiwanICDF online application, separately apply to the chosen TICA university, deliver required documents through your ROC (Taiwan) embassy/representative office, pass the embassy first review (list due around 31 March), pass the university-plus-TaiwanICDF committee second review, then receive the Fund's acceptance letter (in principle by 10 June) and return the signed consent form.
